lead.headline: Lovlina wins boxing gold on her birthday; hockey team beat Pakistan 4–3 to reach the final
lead.byline: THE TRIBUNE · HOCKEY INDIA · DECCAN HERALD · 1–2 OCT
lead.short: Lovlina Borgohain beat China's Bao Ziyi 5–0 in the women's 75kg final on Friday, her 29th birthday, to become only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win Asian Games gold. On Thursday the men's hockey team led Pakistan 3–0, were pegged back to 3–3, and won the semi-final with a last-minute goal from Abhishek.
more: The women's recurve archers beat South Korea 5–3 for India's first Asian Games gold in the event; the men's recurve team lost their final to Korea 1–5 for silver. Nitesh Kumar took silver at 97kg in Greco-Roman wrestling, India's first final in the style since 1962. In sailing, Manu and Prince won India's first skiff silver and Nethra Kumanan took bronze. The women's hockey team play China for gold today at 15:30 IST; on Saturday the cricketers play Pakistan at 10:00 IST and the men's hockey team meet Malaysia at 15:30 IST.

why.text: Three team finals in two days, and the cricket one is against Pakistan.

facts.hockey_finals: women v China 2 Oct, men v Malaysia 3 Oct, 15:30 IST
facts.archery: women's recurve team gold, men's silver

seconds.headline: UEFA presses on with its Barcelona investigation after Madrid hand over a 50,000-page dossier
seconds.short: UEFA confirmed it has received Real Madrid's complaint and documents about the €8.4 million Barcelona paid between 2001 and 2018 to companies linked to José María Enríquez Negreira, then vice-president of Spain's referees' committee, and that its investigation continues. Madrid's statement asked UEFA to proceed with the utmost urgency and act according to the severity of what it finds.
more: Barcelona say nothing new has been opened: UEFA appointed investigators in 2023. A separate Spanish criminal case is heading for trial in 2027.

why.text: The case that hangs over Barcelona's titles of that era is back on UEFA's desk, pushed there by Madrid.

seconds.headline: Ronaldo walks out of Portugal's camp after being dropped; Portugal win in Denmark without him
seconds.byline: AL JAZEERA · ESPN · THE GUARDIAN · 1 OCT
seconds.short: Coach Jorge Jesus said Cristiano Ronaldo would not start in Copenhagen after he spent the win over Norway on the bench; Ronaldo then left the squad, saying on Instagram he would explain his reasons to the Portuguese people in due course. Jesus says there is no rift. Without him Portugal won 4–2 in Copenhagen on Thursday, with Gonçalo Ramos, who has taken his place, scoring one and setting up another; Rasmus Højlund celebrated a Denmark goal with Ronaldo's 'Siu'. Ronaldo has not yet given his reasons, and has not said whether he will play for Portugal again.

why.text: At 41, this may be how Ronaldo's international career ends.

seconds.headline: Over 500 detained at Jantar Mantar as protesters demand the Chief Election Commissioner resign
seconds.byline: THEPRINT · THE HINDU · TIMES OF INDIA · 2 OCT
seconds.short: Delhi Police detained AAP's Atishi, Sanjay Singh and Saurabh Bharadwaj among more than 500 protesters from parties and student groups demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over the voter-roll revision. Mobile internet was cut within 1.5 km of Jantar Mantar from 9:00 to 21:00 and 11 Metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, closed their gates.
more: A Supreme Court judge declined to hear a petition about the CEC and told the petitioners to approach the Chief Justice. In Karnataka, the Commission ordered a probe into bulk Form 7 deletion requests after Chief Minister Shivakumar's six-hour sit-in.

why.text: The row over the Commission has moved from statements to the street, and to the courts.

seconds.headline: HDFC Bank picks ICICI veteran Anup Bagchi as its next chief executive
seconds.short: Bagchi, chief executive of ICICI Prudential Life since 2023 and at the ICICI group since 1992, takes over as managing director and CEO for three years from 27 October. He succeeds Sashidhar Jagdishan, who told the board in August he would not seek another term; the bank had sent the RBI his name and that of deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha.
more: The appointment comes a day after Kotak Mahindra Bank named Anup Kumar Saha as its next CEO, so two of India's three largest private banks change leaders this autumn.

why.text: Your HDFC cards are with the bank changing its chief; nothing changes for customers on the day.

stories.headline: Verstappen fastest in Sepang's first practice, 0.383s clear of Russell
stories.short: Verstappen lapped in 1m37.520s, ahead of George Russell and his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar, as drivers reported very heavy tyre wear on the abrasive surface. Mercedes, who brought their big upgrade, wondered on team radio whether they were the outliers on degradation. Hadjar, Arvid Lindblad and Franco Colapinto will take grid penalties on Sunday for extra power-unit parts.

why.text: A first look that suits Max; qualifying is Saturday at 13:30 IST on FanCode.

preview.text: Sepang's very fast corners and two long straights joined by the Turn 15 hairpin reward a stable, efficient car, and its abrasive surface is eating tyres: drivers called Friday's wear extreme. Mercedes have won the last three races and brought a large upgrade, but were unsure on Friday whether their tyre wear was worse than the rest. Verstappen topped first practice with Hadjar third.

picks.says: Verstappen beat the upgraded Mercedes in the first session, the headline of practice one.
Mercedes, winners of the last three races, look the team to beat with new parts, but Russell faces an engine penalty.

briefs.text: The corridor would take flights from Leh into Chinese airspace near Hotan and on west, saving the one to three hours that detours over the Arabian Sea add; Pakistan's ban runs to 24 October. Talks have gone on for over a year without agreement, and parts of the region's airspace are under Chinese military control.

briefs.headline: Russia is buying back petrol made from its own crude in Indian refineries
briefs.text: With Ukrainian drones knocking out refineries faster than they can be repaired, Russia imports fuel; India supplied 70% of its oil-product imports in August, including 120,000 tonnes of petrol, and Moscow subsidises importers to cover the loss. It matters now because a new US law lets Washington tariff countries buying Russian oil.
